title: standing-gates-the-newest-link-and-run-proof-names-its-sink
intention: Point the seal gate at the question it is actually asked, and give the seal one named sink. standing() asks 'is this proof's code proven RIGHT NOW?' — a question answered entirely by the newest seal: green, its link verifying, its fingerprint matching. It currently refuses on the integrity of the ENTIRE trail, so a stale entry about code that has since moved poisons an answer that does not concern it. And run_proof still returns a record without persisting it, so every caller must remember the door — which is how seven entries came to be written around it.
why: The prior fix (validation-store-door-is-the-only-path, cleared 2026-08-05) did not hold: six trails carry seven unlinked entries dated 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-08, and the trouble stands re-raised at prior_attempts 1. The two halves of this ticket answer the two halves of that failure. THE GENERATOR: run_proof's own docstring says it 'does not persist it (the store is a later stone)' — the store stopped being a later stone on 2026-08-05 and the handoff never closed. `cairn test` makes the gap concrete: it runs proofs, prints greens, and lands nothing, so the only way to make a seal durable is by hand. That is not a lapse of attention, it is the affordance the tool offers. THE READER: the trail-wide gate is a reasoned overshoot, not a response to any measured tamper — the prior ticket's `learned` records that its draft tolerated an unlinked PREFIX, that the proof killed that tolerance, and that 'the fix was to remove the clause rather than narrow it'. Removing was correct about the prefix rule and landed one stop past the right rule. Akien, 2026-08-16, on what a validation IS: 'evidence once we've completed something is irrelevant and tends to cause confusion once the point the evidence is centered around is resolved. we don't need to keep history. we need to keep THIS WORKED LAST TIME I TRIED IT ON yyymmddhhmmssuuuu which is what validations are.' And on the shape of the miss, which is the general one: 'a while back you threw an error because a seive was checking for a file, but the error wasn't that the file wasn't there it was that it didn't have the field. the seive needed to be repointed at the thing it actually needed, not the higher order thing.'

falsifier.proves_green: proof beside the code, sealed under the tester at isolation='netns'; the emit chokepoint validates each crossing and its exit gate demands a complete, passing verdict artifact against the claiming validate berth before PROVED
falsifier.proves_red: Four clauses, each a tooth a hollow build could not pass: (1) a hand-written record — no link, or a link copied from another entry — passes standing() as the newest seal; (2) an in-place edit of an OLDER entry does not break the newest link and standing() still returns proven (the clause that would show the narrowing went too far); (3) run_proof can be called without naming a sink, i.e. a seal can still be silently produced and dropped; (4) a validation trail exists in the corpus whose newest entry carries no verifying link and no proof tooth reds.
falsifier.horizon: at the next tester change, and whenever a new caller of run_proof or of the validation trail is added. Re-declared deliberately from the prior ticket, whose fix did not hold on exactly this horizon.

questions.a: THE NARROWING IS NOT THE KILLED TOLERANCE, BY THAT RULE'S OWN TEST. The prior ticket's general shape is 'a tolerance is a forger's costume whenever the forger can produce the thing being tolerated.' It killed a tolerance of an unlinked leading PREFIX — and a forger can produce an unlinked prefix, since a total overwrite is one, which is why it fell. What is tolerated here is unlinked entries sitting BENEATH a newest link that verifies, and the forger cannot produce the required half: a link that hashes the current prefix comes only from the store's own _link_for, at which point calling the door is cheaper than forging. The rule and this narrowing agree.

THE DIAGNOSTIC IS NOT THE GATE, AND BOTH ARE KEPT. inspect_trail retains all three lanes and keeps checking the whole trail — it localizes a tamper to its earliest entry, which is what a census tooth should print and what complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass wants. Only standing()'s GATING question narrows. The instrument stays as sharp as it is; the gate stops answering a wider question than it was asked.

THE OLD-ENTRY-TAMPER CASE IS COVERED BY THE MERKLE PROPERTY, NOT BY THE TRAIL WALK. test_an_EDIT_to_an_older_entry_breaks_the_newest_link asserts breaks on entry 0 AND entry 1 — entry 1 being the newest — so the top link already catches it. The tooth's docstring claims the tamper is 'invisible to a newest entry reader'; that describes a reader of the newest RECORD's content, which is not what standing() will do.

WHAT WHOLE-TRAIL GATING ACTUALLY BOUGHT, stated so the loss is deliberate: localization of the earliest tamper point (kept — it moves to inspect_trail and the census tooth), and refusal on unlinked OLD entries (dropped on purpose — that is the class Akien ruled irrelevant once the point the evidence centred on is resolved).

THE QUARANTINE DESIGN IS WITHDRAWN AND WHY IT WAS WRONG BEYOND BEING UNNECESSARY. It would have written a ruling-shaped record into the trail permanently — a thing existing only because Akien signed it — at the moment the standing aim is to remove him from the process. 'I HAVE TO BE PART OF THE PROCESS. And we're trying slowly to remove me from the process' (Akien, 2026-08-16). The repointed gate needs no ruling at all, and that is a property of the fix worth naming, not a side effect.

standing()'s PRINTED REMEDY IS FALSE FOR THIS CLASS. It says 'Recover the trail from git and re-run the proof'; measured across every commit of test_host.json, entry 1 arrived unlinked at its first commit and carries no link at any commit. The sentence was written for the destroy-the-history attack and inherited by the never-came-through-the-door case. It is corrected as part of this ticket.

proof: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_validation_store.py — 16 teeth (roster floor raised 11 -> 16), including the four the falsifier names: an unlinked OLD entry under a verifying newest link still stands; a FORGED newest entry cannot borrow a link (no link, and a link copied from entry 0); an edit to an OLDER entry still refuses at standing() (the over-narrowing guard); and the corpus census — every one of the 90 real validation trails in class-space has a newest entry whose link verifies, asserted as an invariant over a population floor of 70 rather than the snapshot 90, and red on both vacuous cases (a known-bad fixture corpus, and an empty glob). cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_tester.py — 8 teeth, roster floor now DERIVED from the module's own '^def test_' declarations rather than typed, including test_run_proof_REQUIRES_a_sink_and_has_no_default_for_it. Both run bare, twice, exit 0, and both are sealed green under the tester at isolation='netns' (seal verdict 'sealed': 1.1.1.1:53 reachable bare, unreachable inside netns). AGAINST THE OLD CODE (Law 8): three teeth observed FAILING against HEAD's validation_store.py and device.py loaded under importlib — the git stash the plan named was unsafe against 24 unrelated modified files, so `git show HEAD:` was used instead, which is the stronger instrument. The other two teeth pass both ways BY DESIGN; they guard against over-narrowing rather than witness the change, and counting them as five would have been the hollow reading.
learned: THE AFFORDANCE WAS THE DEFECT, NOT THE LOCK. The 2026-08-05 fix answered a bypass with three physics layers and every layer held; the corpus routed around them within two days because no reachable path could land a seal at all. What closed it was a required sink and a --seal flag — and, more than either, a non-sealing run that SAYS SO, because a run that printed green and persisted nothing was indistinguishable from one that sealed, which is how eight days of working around the door stayed invisible. THE PROOF WAS DEMANDING THE FALSE SENTENCE: test_a_FORCED_write_cannot_pass_for_a_seal asserted that standing()'s refusal contained 'recover the trail from git' — a remedy that never existed for that case (measured: the unlinked entries arrived unlinked at their first commit). A tooth can hold a lie in place through a whole voyage, and this one did. THREE CHART CLAIMS FALSIFIED BY THE BUILD'S OWN TOOL CALLS: survey said 'two production call sites' for run_proof (24 needed the sink, the rest in proofs/); survey measured 78 validation trails where the census reads 90; and hypothesis 8's expect proposed the snapshot 78 as the census floor while its own falsifier called that out — the falsifier was right and the expect was wrong, which is the useful direction for that pair to disagree in. THE PACKET'S SCORE, READ DOWNWARD (ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap): 120 tool calls between the validate berth and done, against 50 for the whole seven-stage chart chain that produced it. Measured by timestamp against the session transcript, not estimated. Nothing counts this on its own — ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart is the owed observer — so the number is a hand's act and is recorded here rather than narrated. Three of the named falsifications above sit under it as the second layer: a score says the packet was thin, it never says which field was.
